content.title: Pay for an enterprise order
content.description: A Buyer or Procurement Manager settles an order by either submitting a purchase order against the account credit line or paying by corporate card, with PO and card-field validation, credit and per-order card limits, consecutive-failure lockout behavior, and plain-text card-storage prohibition enforced before payment can proceed.
content.summary: Complete payment by PO or corporate card.
content.value: Collects payment using enterprise controls that prevent uncollectible or insecure orders.
criteria: Payment offers exactly two methods: Purchase Order (on account) and Corporate Card.
Purchase Order payment requires a PO number matching `PO-` followed by 6 digits and uses Net 30 terms.
Purchase Order payment is blocked when the order total exceeds the account's available credit of $150,000, and the buyer is directed to use a corporate card or contact the account manager.
Corporate Card accepts Visa, Mastercard, and Amex; validates the card number with a Luhn check; requires a future expiry; and requires CVV of 3 digits, or 4 for Amex.
Corporate Card payment is limited to $10,000 per order, with an above-limit message directing the buyer to use a purchase order.
After 3 consecutive card-authorization failures, the card form is locked for 15 minutes and a support contact is shown.
Card data is never stored in plain text.
